## Body

From the 2026-11-08 run (#166-#189):
- Batch rounds. When several seats review one head, have the coder prepare fixes locally and push ONE round only after every seat at that head has reported. #183 got 14 findings from 3 seats; pushing per finding would have cost 3x the reviewer time.
- Stacked PRs: route the coder's own commit now; the rebase onto the moving base becomes a base-only delta. Merge order follows the stack.
- Send current-work instructions as a normal send, never --fyi. An FYI to an idle or mid-turn seat isn't seen; I lost about 40 minutes once on this.
- When a seat is cold (the cold-wake guard refuses), use --force --reason only if the seat holds the needed context. Otherwise use a warm seat.
- Migrations: main's highest + 1 at push time; first to push wins. Tell the other coders the moment one claims a number.
- Injection class (F132): any caller-, seat- or model-supplied string in daemon-authored text (pij-bg messages, digests, CLI prose and printed commands) must go through pij_core::render (closed grammars, fenced free text). Raw stays only in --json, documented as untrusted. Every reviewer round found another sink; ask for an inventory with a disposition per row.
- Identity GAIN (acting as another seat, or getting its capability) is outside C32(1). A proofless op that erases a live owner's protection must not lead to issuance; require nonce or token.
- Brake vs policy (AGENTS.md): name it in every destructive PR. On error, fail SAFE toward the conservative action (an extra memory turn), not a refusal that strands a seat.
- Verify ocelot's done with `pij report verify`. If the spine doesn't change, its done isn't filed yet.
